subject: botany_2
question_text: Write any four physiological effects of cytokinins in plants.

mark_split.label: What cytokinins are and where they are made

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.26, printed question 22. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: The question asks for FOUR. Number them one to four and stop — an examiner marking four effects will not hunt through a paragraph for the fourth.

steps.label: What cytokinins are
steps.margin_note: Definition, the three sites, one named example.
lines: Cytokinins are plant growth hormones that
promote CELL DIVISION.
They are made where rapid cell division occurs:
root tips, shoot buds and young fruits.
Zeatin is a natural cytokinin.
steps.why: They are made exactly where cells are dividing fastest, which is the clearest evidence of what their main job is.
common_mistakes: Saying cytokinins cause cell elongation. That is auxin and gibberellin; cytokinin causes cell DIVISION.
Saying they are made at the shoot tip only. Root tips, shoot buds and young fruits.
steps.memory_tip: Cytokinin means cell division: kinesis is division.

steps.label: Cell division and new organs
steps.margin_note: Three numbered effects. Keep the numbering going into the next steps.
lines: 1. They promote cell division in root tips and
shoot tips.
2. They help produce new LEAVES and
CHLOROPLASTS in leaves.
3. They help lateral shoot growth and
adventitious shoot formation.
steps.why: New leaves and new chloroplasts both need new cells first, so they follow directly from the cell-division effect.
common_mistakes: Listing only 'cell division'. The question asks for four separate EFFECTS.
Leaving out chloroplast formation. It is one of the named effects.
steps.memory_tip: More divisions means more leaves, and more chloroplasts inside them.

steps.label: Delaying senescence
steps.margin_note: Name the effect and say why it happens. The named effect is a bonus, not required.
lines: 4. They promote nutrient movement into the
leaf, which DELAYS leaf senescence.
A leaf treated with cytokinin stays green while
the leaves around it yellow.
This is called the Richmond-Lang effect.
steps.why: Cytokinin pulls nutrients toward the treated leaf, so that leaf keeps its chlorophyll while untreated leaves lose theirs.
common_mistakes: Saying cytokinins cause yellowing. They DELAY it.
Giving no mechanism. The nutrient movement is what makes the delay happen.
steps.memory_tip: The treated leaf stays green because the food goes to it.

steps.label: Overcoming apical dominance
steps.margin_note: Name the opposition with auxin. That contrast is what earns this mark.

lines.text: Cytokinin releases the buds auxin suppresses

lines: 5. Cytokinins help OVERCOME apical dominance.
They release the lateral buds that auxin from
the shoot tip was suppressing.
So the plant produces side branches and grows
BUSHY.
steps.why: Auxin and cytokinin work against each other on the same lateral buds, so raising the cytokinin has the same effect as removing the auxin source.
common_mistakes: Saying cytokinin causes apical dominance. Auxin causes it; cytokinin OVERCOMES it.
Leaving out the bushy growth. That is the visible result.
steps.memory_tip: Auxin holds the side buds down; cytokinin lets them up.
